newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end up on power stocks, trade anemic.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end up on power stocks, trade anemic.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended slightly higher led by continuing rises in electrical sector shares but trade was anemic as many foreign investors were absent due to the Columbus Day holiday in the United States, brokers said.
"Forget about any comments today," one dealer said. "There is nothing to report."
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 49 most traded shares edged up 226 points, or 0.34 percent, to close at 66,313 points on weak volume of 241 million reais ($235.2 million.)
Brokers said trade plummeted from Friday's volume of more than 400 million reais, remaining heavly concentrated in shares of federal telecoms giant Telebras.
The bolsa was down most of the day, except for power sector shares, which continued rising to build on last week's strong rally on the sector's good prospects for privatization.
The Bovespa rose in late trade as investors picked up benchmark Telebras preferred shares with an eye on next Monday's options settlements.
Market volatility is expected to rise this week as options expiry nears, especially after futures settlements on Wednesday.
Among blue-chips, Telebras preferred closed 0.37 percent higher at 81.00 reais and its voting common dipped 0.58 percent to 68.00 reais.
The day's rise was led by electric company stocks again, building on last week's strong gains.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index (IEE) of nine most-liquid power stocks surged 1.94 percent to end at 1,758 points.
State power firm Eletrobras's common was the top gainer, rising 2.3 percent to end at 311.00 reais, while its blue-chip preferred.
Minas Gerais state electrical firm Cemig rose 2.08 percent to end at 49.00 reais and its preferred rose 1.18 percent to 34.40 reais.
Meanwhile, state miner Cia Vale do Rio Doce preferred fell 0.48 percent to close at 20.65 reais while its voting common dropped 3.46 percent to 25.10 reais.
State oil firm Petrobras' preferred rose 0.42 percent to 121.50 reais while its common share ended 0.75 percent lower at 79.00 reais -- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
